def-finite-probability-vector:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty set. A **probability vector** on
$\mathcal X$ is a family $P=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$ of real numbers such that
$p_x\ge 0$ for every $x$ and $\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x=1$. Its support is
$\operatorname{supp}P:=\{x\in\mathcal X:p_x>0\}$. Coordinates outside the
support are retained as zeros; they are not deleted from the alphabet.

For another probability vector $Q=(q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$, the notation
$P\ll Q$ means $\operatorname{supp}P\subseteq\operatorname{supp}Q$. All
finite sums over $\mathcal X$ use the displayed alphabet and ordinary finite
real arithmetic, extended to $+\infty$ only where a later definition says so.
lem-convex-generator-boundary-limits-exi:
## Statement

Let $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be convex and satisfy $f(1)=0$. Then $f$
is continuous on $(0,\infty)$, and both extended-real limits
$$f(0):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t),\qquad f_\infty:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(t)}t$$
exist in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$; neither limit is $-\infty$.
lem-finite-kl-generator-is-admissible:
## Statement

For $f(t)=t\log t$ on $t>0$, one has $f(1)=0$, $f$ is convex on
$(0,\infty)$, $\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t)=0$, and
$\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t=+\infty$.
lem-finite-renyi-generators-are-convex:
## Statement

For $\alpha>1$, the generator $h_\alpha(t)=t^\alpha-1$ is convex on
$(0,\infty)$, satisfies $h_\alpha(1)=0$, has
$h_\alpha(0+)=-1$, and has recession limit
$\lim_{t\to\infty}h_\alpha(t)/t=+\infty$. For $0<\alpha<1$, the generator
$g_\alpha(t)=1-t^\alpha$ is convex on $(0,\infty)$, satisfies
$g_\alpha(1)=0$, has $g_\alpha(0+)=1$, and has recession limit
$\lim_{t\to\infty}g_\alpha(t)/t=0$.
def-finite-f-divergence:
## Definition

Let $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty
alphabet $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]). A **convex
generator** is a finite convex function $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ with
$f(1)=0$; convexity uses the two-point inequality of
[[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]]. Use its
extended boundary values
$$f(0):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t),\qquad f_\infty:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(t)}t.$$
These limits exist in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ by
[[lem-convex-generator-boundary-limits-exist]]. Define the **finite
f-divergence from $P$ to $Q$**
by
$$D_f(P\|Q):=\sum_{x:q_x>0}q_x f(p_x/q_x)+ f_\infty\sum_{x:q_x=0}p_x.$$
In the first sum, if $p_x=0$, the term means $q_x f(0)$. A coordinate with
$p_x=q_x=0$ contributes zero and is omitted. The second term is defined as
zero when its coefficient $\sum_{q_x=0}p_x$ is zero, even if
$f_\infty=+\infty$; if that coefficient is positive and $f_\infty=+\infty$,
the divergence is $+\infty$.

The boundary term is essential when $P\not\ll Q$. It is the recession
contribution of the generator and is not the value $f(0)$.
def-finite-hypothesis-testing-beta:
## Definition

Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$
([[def-finite-probability-vector]]). They define finite probability spaces
with outcome weights $p_x$ and $q_x$, respectively
([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). For $h:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$, write
$E_Ph:=\sum_xp_xh(x)$ and $E_Qh:=\sum_xq_xh(x)$; these are the finite
expectations ([[def-expectation-on-a-finite-probability-space]]). Test the
simple null $H_0:P$ against the simple alternative $H_1:Q$. A randomized test is a function
$\phi:\mathcal X\to[0,1]$, where $\phi(x)$ is the probability of rejecting
$H_0$ after observing $x$; thus $1-\phi(x)$ is the probability of accepting
$H_0$ ([[def-randomized-test]]). Its type-I error is
$\sum_xp_x\phi(x)$, and its type-II error is
$\sum_xq_x(1-\phi(x))$ ([[def-test-size-and-power]]).

For $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, define the oriented type-II testing function
$$\beta_\epsilon(P,Q):=\inf_{\substack{\phi:\mathcal X\to[0,1]\\\sum_xp_x\phi(x)\le\epsilon}}\sum_xq_x(1-\phi(x)).$$
Here the first argument is the null law and the second is the alternative
law; $\epsilon$ bounds rejection under the first law, while the objective is
acceptance of the null under the second. The feasible set is nonempty
because $\phi=0$ is allowed, and every objective value lies in $[0,1]$, so
the infimum is a real number in that interval. In the
Neyman–Pearson-region convention that constrains null acceptance below by
$\gamma$, this is the lower boundary value at $\gamma=1-\epsilon$.
def-finite-stochastic-kernel:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be finite nonempty sets. A **stochastic kernel**
from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ is a matrix
$K=(K(y\mid x))_{x\in\mathcal X,y\in\mathcal Y}$ such that
$K(y\mid x)\ge0$ and $\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}K(y\mid x)=1$ for every
$x\in\mathcal X$. The convention is input first in the condition and output
first in the value $K(y\mid x)$.

For a probability vector $P=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$, the output vector
$PK$ on $\mathcal Y$ is
$$(PK)_y:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xK(y\mid x).$$
It is a probability vector because its coordinates are nonnegative and
$\sum_y(PK)_y=\sum_xp_x\sum_yK(y\mid x)=\sum_xp_x=1$.
def-finite-kullback-leibler-divergence:
## Definition

For probability vectors $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ on the same finite
nonempty alphabet, their **Kullback–Leibler divergence** (or **relative
entropy**) in the stated direction from $P$ to $Q$ is
$$D(P\|Q):=\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x\log\frac{p_x}{q_x}.$$
The logarithm is natural. If $p_x>0$ and $q_x=0$ for at least one $x$, set
$D(P\|Q)=+\infty$. If $p_x=0$, its contribution is zero, including when
$q_x=0$; equivalently, $0\log(0/q_x)=0$. When $P\ll Q$, all ratios in the
sum are positive and finite.

The generator $f(t)=t\log t$ is admissible for
[[def-finite-f-divergence]] by
[[lem-finite-kl-generator-is-admissible]]. Its boundary values
$f(0)=0$ and $f_\infty=+\infty$ make that f-divergence exactly the displayed
KL formula, including the singular-support case.
lem-convex-perspective-is-subadditive:
## Statement

Let $f$ be a convex generator from [[def-finite-f-divergence]]. Define its
closed perspective on $a,b\ge0$ by
$$\Pi_f(a,b):=\begin{cases} b f(a/b),&b>0,\ a>0,\\ b f(0),&b>0,\ a=0,\\ a f_\infty,&b=0,\ a>0,\\ 0,&a=b=0. \end{cases}$$
For every finite family $(a_i,b_i)\in[0,\infty)^2$,
$$\Pi_f\!\left(\sum_i a_i,\sum_i b_i\right)\le\sum_i\Pi_f(a_i,b_i).$$
def-finite-renyi-divergence:
## Definition

Let $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ be probability vectors on the same finite
nonempty alphabet. For order $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ with $\alpha\ne1$, put
$$S_\alpha(P,Q):=\sum_{x:q_x>0}p_x^\alpha q_x^{1-\alpha}.$$
If $\alpha>1$ and $p_x>0=q_x$ for some $x$, define
$S_\alpha(P,Q)=+\infty$; if $0<\alpha<1$, such coordinates contribute
zero. In the displayed sum, $p_x=0<q_x$ contributes zero. If the sum is
zero, then necessarily $\alpha<1$ and the logarithmic expression below is
defined as $+\infty$. The **Rényi divergence of order $\alpha$ from $P$ to
$Q$** is
$$D_\alpha(P\|Q):=\frac{\log S_\alpha(P,Q)}{\alpha-1}.$$
At order one define
$$D_1(P\|Q):=D(P\|Q),$$
using [[def-finite-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. All divergences are
extended-real-valued; the direction is always first argument to second.

For $0<\alpha<1$, a point with $p_x>0=q_x$ contributes zero to the affinity
$S_\alpha$ rather than infinity. For $\alpha>1$, the same support mismatch
makes $D_\alpha(P\|Q)=+\infty$. The sign of $\alpha-1$ is part of the
definition and reverses inequalities when $0<\alpha<1$.
lem-finite-iid-log-likelihood-concentrat:
## Statement

Let $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty
alphabet with $P\ll Q$. For $n\ge1$, write
$P^n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_i p_{x_i}$ and
$Q^n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_i q_{x_i}$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent
with common law $P$, define $\ell(x)=\log(p_x/q_x)$ when $p_x>0$ and
$\ell(x)=0$ when $p_x=0$, and put $L_n=\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(X_i)$. Then
$L_n/n\to D(P\|Q)$ in probability as $n\to\infty$. For every
$x^n\in\operatorname{supp}(P)^n$, one also has
$Q^n(x^n)=P^n(x^n)\exp(-L_n(x^n))$.
thm-finite-f-divergence-data-processing:
## Statement

Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$,
let $K$ be a stochastic kernel from $\mathcal X$ to a finite nonempty
alphabet $\mathcal Y$, and let $f$ be a convex generator as in
[[def-finite-f-divergence]]. Then
$$D_f(PK\|QK)\le D_f(P\|Q),$$
with both divergences interpreted using the zero and singular-support
conventions of that definition.
thm-finite-kullback-leibler-data-process:
## Statement

For probability vectors $P,Q$ on a finite nonempty alphabet and a stochastic
kernel $K$ to another finite nonempty alphabet,
$$D(PK\|QK)\le D(P\|Q).$$
thm-finite-renyi-data-processing:
## Statement

Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$
and let $K$ be a stochastic kernel from $\mathcal X$ to a finite nonempty
alphabet $\mathcal Y$. For every $\alpha\in(0,\infty)\setminus\{1\}$,
$$D_\alpha(PK\|QK)\le D_\alpha(P\|Q),$$
with Rényi divergence as defined in [[def-finite-renyi-divergence]].
thm-finite-renyi-limit-is-kullback-leibl:
## Statement

For probability vectors $P,Q$ on a finite nonempty alphabet,
$$\lim_{\alpha\to1}D_\alpha(P\|Q)=D(P\|Q)$$
as a two-sided extended-real limit.
thm-kl-is-iid-type-ii-error-exponent:
## Statement

Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$.
For $n\ge1$, write $P^n,Q^n$ for the product vectors on $\mathcal X^n$,
with $P^n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_{i=1}^np_{x_i}$ and similarly for $Q^n$.
For every fixed $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, with $\beta_\epsilon$ oriented as in
[[def-finite-hypothesis-testing-beta]],
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}-\frac1n\log\beta_\epsilon(P^n,Q^n)=D(P\|Q),$$
where $-\log0:=+\infty$.
